passage: Karthik wheeled his new bicycle to the tea stall at the end of the lane, its bell still wrapped in plastic. Nilesh could not stop looking at it. Karthik wanted someone to play tag with, but Nilesh only wanted the bicycle. Karthik thought for a moment. "You take the first turn, to the neem tree and back. After that, we play tag." Nilesh grinned and climbed on. He rang the bell twice, went to the tree and back, and handed it over. "Now tag," he said. "You are it!" The lane filled with running feet.

qa.q: What did Karthik offer Nilesh first?
qa.a: Karthik offered Nilesh the first turn on the bicycle, to the neem tree and back.

qa.q: What did Karthik want from Nilesh, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Karthik wanted someone to play tag with. He stopped to think and then made an offer instead of just asking.

qa.q: What other approach could Karthik try if Nilesh said no to the trade, and why?
qa.a: He could copy how other children ask, by saying "Can I play tag with you?" with a smile. It costs nothing and may work on its own.

qa.q: How does the offer look to Nilesh?
qa.a: Nilesh gets the thing he most wants right away, and playing tag is a small price. That is why he grins.

grounding: A child trades the first turn on the new bicycle for a game of tag afterwards.
